item.text: {"question_id":"1B.3","answer":"For China in 2023, the evidence shows a mixed and incompletely verified nuclear-control posture. A historical safeguard was concentrated launch authority: both the Politburo Standing Committee and Central Military Commission had to agree to alert or launch, while warheads were generally stored separately from dispersed missiles at low peacetime readiness (BATCH-0025-E029). SIPRI likewise reported that peacetime warheads were widely believed to be stored separately and not immediately launch-ready, but supplied no inspection or enforcement evidence (BATCH-0017-E008). During Xi’s tenure, however, China increased nuclear readiness and adopted more distributed warhead-handling practices; the possible future shift toward launch-on-warning remained unresolved, and available evidence did not clarify whether launch procedures and authorities had been adapted to shortened warning times (BATCH-0025-E029). Xi would have had to approve changes to the nuclear forces, and a Chinese scholar attributed personal planning of strategic-force construction to him, but the evidence does not establish his specific command-safety decisions or corrective actions (BATCH-0025-E031). FAS further reported uncertainty about the operational status of new silos because support facilities, command-and-control systems, and security perimeters were still being completed (BATCH-0023-E009). China’s 2023 UN submissions addressed nuclear risk reduction and safeguards, but the supplied records contain only metadata and do not show substantive implementation (BATCH-0012-E004; BATCH-0012-E012). Accordingly, the record supports some formal or inherited central-control and custody arrangements, but does not demonstrate that Xi funded, staffed, inspected, enforced, or corrected nuclear safety safeguards effectively.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0025-E029","BATCH-0017-E008","BATCH-0023-E009","BATCH-0025-E031","BATCH-0012-E004","BATCH-0012-E012"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0025-E029","BATCH-0025-E031","BATCH-0023-E009","BATCH-0017-E008"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied evidence does not provide a verified 2023 nuclear accident, near-miss, inspection result, enforcement action, staffing record, or corrective-action record.","The storage and command arrangements are partly described as widely believed, estimated, or inferential, with no direct inspection evidence.","The evidence does not establish whether Xi personally directed the specific safety, custody, inspection, or corrective measures discussed.","The UN working-paper records show only that China submitted papers addressing nuclear-risk-reduction or safeguards topics; the supplied extracts do not show their substantive proposals or implementation.","The supplied critical-infrastructure cybersecurity regulation is not treated as evidence of nuclear command-and-control, custody, or accident-prevention effectiveness."] ,"corrections_made":["Removed the critical-infrastructure cybersecurity regulations from the substantive support for nuclear safeguards.","Recast separate storage as reported or widely believed practice rather than demonstrated effective safety.","Preserved the contrary evidence on increased readiness, distributed warhead handling, possible launch-on-warning, incomplete command-and-control infrastructure, and possible narrowing of expert influence.","Tightened attribution by distinguishing Xi’s formal authority and an attributed scholar’s claim of personal planning from proof of specific command-safety action.","Separated formal submissions and inherited arrangements from demonstrated implementation, enforcement, inspection, or correction."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A full ledger review would be warranted if direct evidence of nuclear inspections, command staffing, safety incidents, enforcement, corrective actions, or Xi-specific operational orders becomes available."]}
